title: Students march to Kalady university after Kerala High Court revokes suspensions
seoTitle: Kalady students march after suspension revoked

tea.why: Students were protesting against their 84-day suspension from the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit following campus demonstrations.
tea.want: Reinstatement of suspended students, withdrawal of apology requirements, and fulfillment of an 18-point charter of demands.
tea.changed: Nov 23: The Kerala High Court set aside the suspensions, allowing 16 students to end their 22-day relay hunger strike and return to campus.

summary: On November 23, 2026, 16 students from the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (SSUS) in Kalady held a victory march to return to campus. This followed a Kerala High Court order that revoked their suspensions, which had lasted 84 days. The students, affiliated with the Students Federation of India (SFI), had been conducting a 22-day relay hunger strike at a protest pandal outside the university. CPI(M) district secretary S. Satish formally ended the hunger strike by offering the students juice. While the specific hunger strike concluded, the SFI stated that a broader, 124-day-old agitation would continue until the university addresses an 18-point charter of demands. The students rejected demands for an apology, characterizing the court verdict as a vindication of their position against the university administration and state government.
response: The Kerala High Court ordered the immediate reinstatement of the 16 suspended students. No other official response from the university or government regarding the broader 18-point list of demands was reported in the sources.

updates.text: The Kerala High Court ordered the reinstatement of 16 suspended students, leading to the conclusion of a 22-day relay hunger strike.
